evidence.appropriate: the persona's sock puppet, mouth open mid-word; but the beaked head can read as a dinosaur or bird before a friend
evidence.distinctive: probe 0 of 20 for "hand puppet logo" (glove-puppet bears, marionette hands, no profile sock); no competitor uses a puppet
evidence.simple: a sleeve, a long rounded head, one wedge mouth and one eye; 17 anchors
evidence.legible: the silhouette survives to 16 px, but at 24 and 16 px it can read as a letter F
evidence.adaptable: one colour and reversed both hold; the mouth gives an obvious motion (it talks when the child reads)
evidence.timeless: no trend shape; a flat silhouette that would have read the same ten years ago
evidence.universal: mirrored is clean; the profile can read as a small dinosaur or bird, a secondary reading; rotated 90 is abstract
evidence.clear: description search found Smith Micro's 2013 Sock Puppets app and the Burlington Sock Puppets team mark, neither a silhouette like this; Lens skipped (owner decision)
evidence.congruent: round forms, asymmetric gesture (the open mouth), medium filled weight, open frame; small and quick like 'Pip'
evidence.system: horizontal, stacked, symbol, compact, small and favicon all build; the silhouette echoes the P of the wordmark

reconciled.appropriate: I lowered 5 to 4 after the critic's dinosaur-or-bird reading, which I had noted under universal; the puppet persona still reads without a caption, so 4, not 3
reconciled.legible: I lowered 5 to 4 after the critic's F reading at 24 and 16 px; the silhouette holds as one shape with an open mouth at 16 px, so 4 stands over 3
